summary: vite-plugin-crypto fetches and executes remote code on plugin load
details: vite-plugin-crypto advertises build-time AES-GCM encryption but its exported cryptoPlugin() factory concatenates three caller-supplied option fields (secret + salt + iv), base64-decodes the result into a URL, fetches that URL, and executes the response body via `new Function('require','module','exports', code)` using the plugin's own require. The same code path is present in dist/index.cjs (around line 63) and dist/index.js (around line 32), and the errors are swallowed in a try/catch so failures are silent. This code runs whenever a project's vite.config.js imports the plugin and instantiates it, giving whoever controls the decoded URL arbitrary code execution with full Node privileges inside the developer's build. The runtime-reconstructed destination and Function-eval of fetched code are unrelated to the advertised AES-GCM functionality and hide the true endpoint from static review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
